rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **Electric charge** is the fundamental property behind electric forces: two kinds (positive, negative), like repelling and unlike attracting. Its defining properties: **additivity** (charges sum algebraically), **quantisation** — free charge is always an integer multiple of e = 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ C, so 2.5e can never be observed because charge travels in discrete electron/proton packets (NEB 2021, 3m) — and **conservation**,…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - q = ne; e = 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ C - n = q/e (electron count)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Charging never creates charge** — it transfers electrons, leaving equal opposite charge behind.  ·  **q = ne only:** 2.5e, 0.5e are impossible for free matter.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Grounding must be removed BEFORE withdrawing the inducing charged body; otherwise, mobile charges equalize back through ground, leaving the sphere neutral.  ·  Repulsion is the only sure test of electrification because an uncharged body can be attracted by a charged body due to electrostatic polarization.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Comb picking paper*** — electron transfer by friction leaves the comb negative.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Covers only: electric charges (within Electric Charges).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Physics — don't mix them.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Draw sequential schematic diagrams showing charging a conductor by induction.  ·  Calculate electron deficiency or excess for a given charge magnitude.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "n = q/e — and state that n must be an integer."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (2m): A body has a charge of +3.2×10⁻¹⁹ C... possible?** — q/e = 3.2×10⁻¹⁹/1.6×10⁻¹⁹ = 2 → q = +2e: possible (integer multiple).

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Mention quarks only as confined fractional charges — free particles have integer e.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Quantisation + conservation + additivity** — the three pillars of electrostatics.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: q = ne; e = 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ C; like repel, unlike attract; charge is conserved.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: One coulomb corresponds to 6.25×10¹⁸ elementary charges — enormous on the atomic scale.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Like charges → B  ·  Rubbing transfers → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Spark That Starts Electricity Rub a balloon on your hair and it sticks to the wall. That invisible "something" is electric charge — a fundamental property of matter, quantised in units of e, conserved in every interaction, and the protagonist of all of electrostatics.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2021) ### 2.1 Electric charge and its properties - **Charge** is the intrinsic property of matter responsible for electric forces; carried by protons (+e) and electrons (−e). - **Two kinds:** positive and negative — like charges repel, unlike attract. - **Additivity:** total charge is the algebraic sum of individual charges.…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To Topic 85:** Coulomb's law quantifies the force between these charges. - **To atomic structure:** protons/electrons carry ±e; the neutron carries none. - **To nuclear physics (Unit 26):** charge conservation rules every nuclear reaction.

rows.text: Verified PYQ: quantisation + why 2.5e impossible (2021, 3m).  ·  "All free charges are integral multiples of a basic unit of charge e = 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ C."  ·  Why does a rubbed comb attract neutral paper?
